messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Multiple imputation in lavaan
parts:
Hi All,

I would like to ask one quick question about doing multiple imputation (MI) in lavaan.

For people new to MI in lavaan, are there any options other than runMI() and its wrappers from semTools?

runMI() and its wrappers are good tools. I just want to know whether there other options that I overlooked, such that I can compare different options. I searched the Internet and most of the entries refer to runMI() and its wrappers.

Thanks.

Regards,
Shu Fai

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation in lavaan
parts:
With the caveat that I haven't actually tested any of these. I think both the mice and mitml packages would allow you to fit models to multiple imputations (using the with() function in both packages) and then pool results. They should work well for parameter estimates and mitml should work for model comparisons, to get model fit with either it will take a little more work. There are probably other options out there too.

Alex

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation in lavaan
parts: I haven't heard about mitml. I will take a look at it.

It's a great package by a great group of researchers, useful also for standard and multilevel regression.  I use it in my teaching.  They also implemented the latest pooled LRT statistic, which is less computationally intensive, and it indeed works with lavaan models.

https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/d459g

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation in lavaan
parts:
Thanks a lot for the paper! I would take some time to learn more about this package.

If I do multiple imputation mainly in SEM conducted by lavaan and I need to choose one package, for now, would you suggest investing time on runMI() in semTools? Or should I start with mitml, even just for doing analysis in lavaan? runMI() is "for lavaan" and so I can expect better compatibility with lavaan. However, it seems that mitml has more options in doing MI-specific analysis.

Regards,
Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝)
